newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe, Chirac sink further in French poll.
newsitem.headline: Juppe, Chirac sink further in French poll.

text.p: The popularity of French President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe has sunk even lower amid disquiet at record unemployment and their austerity policies, according to an opinion poll issued on Thursday.

The IPSOS survey for the weekly Le Point said only 32 percent of French adults had a favourable view of Chirac, down from 36 percent a month earlier, and just 26 percent had a good opinion of Juppe, down from 31 percent.
But opposition Socialist leader Lionel Jospin failed to benefit from their growing unpopularity, with his own rating falling to 36 percent from 39 percent in September, IPSOS said.
Juppe insisted on Wednesday that he planned to stick to his task "with calmness and determination" despite the low ratings.
"These polls show that that public opinion does not trust the government" he said in an interview on France 3 television.

"For my part, I trust the French, their realism, their common sense and I am convinced that the more we explain our measures...and as people see the first results, we will understand each other better."
IPSOS said it polled 952 adults on October 18-19.
